method: GRADER_PROMPT.md; filters + hours + price visible; median of every reviewer's vote per case

atl-authentic-southern.reason: Mary Mac's at #1 is right and most of the list is real soul food, but for an 'authentic' ask it includes Hattie B's (a Nashville hot-chicken chain) and The Chastain (an upscale Buckhead restaurant, not a Southern specialist, ranked #2 ahead of better-reviewed soul spots), and the best-known authentic soul-food spot is missing.

atl-best-southern-lower.reason: Mostly legitimate soul food with Mary Mac's at #1, but The Chastain (upscale New American, 811 reviews) at #2 is a poor answer to 'best authentic southern', and the obvious canonical pick Busy Bee Cafe is missing.

atl-southern-food.reason: Mary Mac's, Southern Queenz, Twisted Soul, This Is It! and Kenny's Cafe are legitimate Southern/soul answers; The Chastain at #2 is the one weak fit.

tokyo-things.reason: 3 of the top 8 aren't in Tokyo (Fushimi Inari and Kinkaku-ji are in Kyoto, Osaka Castle is in Osaka, all 230+ mi away, with Fushimi Inari at #3 and in the national-icons strip), and the 'regional must-see' strip is filler (Iidabashi Sakura Terrace, Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building) while real Tokyo icons are missing.

paris-museums.reason: Orsay, the Louvre, the Orangerie, Arts Décoratifs, Musée d'Art Moderne and Arts et Métiers are a strong central-Paris museum list (Pompidou is closed for renovation, so leaving it out is fair).

naples-pizza.reason: Port'Alba and the two Sorbillo-family spinoffs are fair picks, but the canonical famous Naples pizzerias are absent from a list sorted by rating and review count, while an obscure 'Pizza fritta' sits at #2.
missing: Gino e Toto Sorbillo (Via dei Tribunali)

statue-bare.reason: The statue itself is first, followed by the Statue of Liberty Museum on the island and the Battery Park lookout, which is exactly what this search should return.

theater-not-food.reason: Correctly returns theaters rather than food, but a shopping mall (The Shops at Santa Anita) sits at #2, and the list is all cinemas with no live-stage option for a 'things to do' theater search.

great-views-not-food.reason: The results are real viewpoints, but most are obscure roadside pullouts with 14-24 reviews and generic names like 'View Point', and the list pads out with spots 28-32 mi away (including Huntington Beach), while the area's well-known view spots are missing.

tokyo-ramen.reason: The #1 result is a 3.7-rated ramen food court in an Odaiba mall, and the top 5 include tourist-oriented halal wagyu spots and a burger/steak restaurant; only Tsujita and a couple of others are credible picks for Tokyo's best ramen.

london-fish-chips.reason: Every result is a real central-London fish and chip shop, led by the well-known Seashell of Lisson Grove with Fishers and Joseph's as solid picks; the high-review tourist chippies (Hobson's, Ben's, Fishoria) are acceptable, though Poppies and the Golden Hind would also be expected.

germany-beer.reason: Munich is a fair reading of a country-wide beer question, and Hofbräuhaus, Löwenbräukeller, Hofbräukeller, Waldwirtschaft and Giesinger are the beer halls and gardens a traveler would expect; Augustiner is a notable absence but the list holds up.

madrid-capital.reason: The app correctly resolved 'capital of Spain' to Madrid, and the top four are classic Madrid institutions (Botín, Lhardy, Casa Lucio, Horcher) followed by well-rated tapas spots; only the Loca Obsesión brunch café is filler.

thailand-street-food.reason: Jay Fai, Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu and the Bamrung Mueang food court fit, but the list also includes a coffee stand that is closed today, a sit-down vegetarian restaurant and a generic Khao San café, and the famous Bangkok street-food names are missing.

vegas-buffets.reason: Bacchanal and the Wynn buffet are the right kind of answer, but two all-you-can-eat sushi/BBQ restaurants rank #2-3 and the rest are off-Strip local Asian buffets, while famous Strip casino buffets are missing.

nyc-brunch.reason: Apart from Barney Greengrass, the list is high-review Midtown tourist spots (a bar and grill, a diner, hotel-area cafés) that no seasoned New Yorker would call the best brunch, and the city's famous brunch institutions are missing.

tokyo-affordable.reason: Mostly fair cheap eats (gyukatsu, Tsujita tsukemen, Age.3, izakaya) that pass the $$ filter, but a novelty maid cafe at #2 is not a 'delicious food' answer and the list is a narrow Akihabara/Ginza slice with none of Tokyo's iconic budget staples.

g-cdmx-markets.reason: Three of eight results including #1 are City Market upscale supermarket branches and La Ciudadela is a crafts market, so only Coyoacán, San Juan and the small weekly markets actually answer 'food markets'.

g-london-quiet-cafe.reason: These are just the nearest West End cafes to Trafalgar Square, not picked for quiet; the busy Crypt cafeteria and tiny Soho coffee bars are poor places for a video call.

g-rome-walking-tours.reason: The top five are real walking-tour operators, but #6 is a generic listing just called 'Rome' 3 mi out and #7 has only 2 reviews, and the best-known Rome guiding companies are absent.

g-istanbul-landmarks.reason: Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque, Dolmabahçe, Basilica Cistern and the Hippodrome monuments are exactly the historic core a traveler expects, though Topkapı Palace should have made the top eight.

g-salsa-clubs.reason: The top results are Old Havana cafes, restaurants and cocktail bars (El Dandy, Antojos, Floridita) rather than salsa dance venues; only 1830 and Tropicana are near the ask, and Havana's main salsa club is missing.

g-lisbon-dessert.reason: Pastéis de Belém, Versailles and Confeitaria Nacional are right, but international ice-cream chains (Amorino, Häagen-Dazs) and gelato are not 'famous local desserts', and the best-known pastel de nata spot downtown is missing.

g-rome-gelato.reason: Giolitti is a fair #1, but the list leans on Trevi-area tourist gelaterie (Gelato g Italiano, Gelato in Trevi) and leaves out the artisan shops Romans and food writers actually name as the best.

near-tiramisu.reason: An Italian pastry shop and Italian restaurants that serve tiramisu lead the list; Jim's Burgers at #6 is the only odd one out.

near-coffee.reason: Eight real coffee shops, all within a mile, nearest first.

near-best-tacos.reason: All taquerias or Mexican taco spots in the San Gabriel Valley, close by and well reviewed.

atmosphere-not-atm.reason: Only five generic cafes about 5 mi away; 'cozy' is matched as a keyword, and a busy boba counter like Bopomofo is not a cozy-atmosphere pick.

charge-phone-not-pho.reason: Convenience stores and pharmacies sell chargers but are not places to sit and charge, and the results lack distance and address data.

cheap-eats.reason: All $-priced, well-reviewed cheap eats within about 2 mi; the price filter was clearly honored.

rooftop-bar.reason: Only Hipico Rooftop is a rooftop bar; the rest are ordinary nearby bars plus an Elks Lodge and an Indian restaurant despite the bars-only filter (unsure of other true rooftop bars nearby).

souvenirs.reason: Generic gift shops, Sanrio character stores, a 1-review shop and an East LA craft store; nothing that sells local Arcadia or LA mementos.
missing: Los Angeles County Arboretum gift shop (exact name unsure)

taipei-night-market.reason: Ningxia, Nanjichang and Guangzhou St are real night markets, but the two most famous are missing and Ximending, Qingguang and Linjiang (morning hours) top the list.

ramen-at-hotel.reason: Good ramen shops, but most are 13-24 mi away in West LA, Hollywood and Little Tokyo, which is not 'near my hotel' in Arcadia.

atv-hawaii.reason: The top five are moped, Slingshot and car rentals, not ATV tours; the actual ATV answers (Coral Crater, Kualoa Ranch) sit at #7-8.

nyc-kids-2-6.reason: Children's Museum of Manhattan fits, but six of eight results are New Jersey mall play spaces rather than NYC toddler staples.

older-teens.reason: Escape rooms, sim racing, laser tag, rage room and immersive exhibits are solid older-teen activities within reach.

tokyo-matcha.reason: Dedicated matcha cafés in Ginza, Tsukiji and Ueno; a fair answer, though classic tea houses like Ippodo aren't shown.

tokyo-fresh-sushi.reason: Tourist-oriented sushi with a conveyor chain (Kura) and a vegan veggie-sushi shop that contradicts 'fresh catch'; nothing tied to the fish market.

la-pancakes.reason: The Griddle Cafe, Du-par's and Gram's souffle pancakes are the right kind of answers, though Pancakes R Us 22 mi away at #2 is a stretch.

la-pancakes-full.reason: Same list: The Griddle Cafe, Du-par's and Gram's souffle pancakes answer the ask, with Pancakes R Us 22 mi away as the odd pick.

bohol-zipline.reason: Bohol's main zipline parks (Chocolate Hills Adventure Park, Danao/EAT, Loboc Eco Adventure Park) are present; a viewing deck, a waterfall and a café are filler.

paris-croissant.reason: Mostly sandwich and brunch cafés, a crêperie, a matcha bar and a banh mi shop; only Union Boulangerie and Brigat' are serious viennoiserie, and the renowned bakeries are missing.

london-strawberries.reason: The Portobello chocolate-strawberry stall and chocolatiers fit, but a sandwich shop at #2, a tea store and a froyo shop are noise.

spain-seniors.reason: Returns municipal senior centers and adult day-care facilities, not activities for senior travelers.

sd-seafood.reason: El Pescador, Tom Ham's, Water Grill and Nico's fit, but a steakhouse at #3 and an Italian restaurant at #5 are junk, and the signature seafood spots are missing.

sd-marketside.reason: Point Loma Seafoods at #1 is exactly right, but the rest are mostly Gaslamp steakhouses, an Italian restaurant and a Filipino supermarket.

la-steamed-crabs.reason: Mostly crab-boil specialists (Boiling Crab, L.A. Crazy Crab, Crab Avenue) plus seafood markets, which fits steamed or cooked crab.

redondo-crabs.reason: Quality Seafood (steams live crabs on the pier) at #1 plus other pier seafood spots is exactly the local answer; only the shabu-shabu place is a stray.

la-beaches.reason: Solid beaches follow, but #1 is 'Beaches Tropicana', a West Hollywood bar, and the most famous LA beaches are missing.

nyc-view.reason: Some picks have views (The View, Bar 54, Duomo51), but it is mostly Midtown bars, a members-only lounge and La Grande Boucherie (no view), and the signature view restaurants are missing.

cebu-view.reason: Some rooftop picks fit, but the list is mostly small, little-reviewed downtown places plus an aquarium dining room, and it misses the well-known hillside view restaurants in Busay and Nivel Hills.

la-beachside.reason: These are genuine oceanfront spots in Santa Monica, Marina del Rey, Playa del Rey and the Palisades (Gladstones, Back on the Beach, Big Dean's, The Albright); the distance is unavoidable for an LA beach ask.

sd-beachside.reason: Most results are on the downtown harbor or bay (Harbor Dr, Harbor Island, Shelter Island, Mission Bay), not the beach, so the classic La Jolla, Pacific Beach and Del Mar beachfront restaurants are missing.

seattle-beachside.reason: These are mostly downtown waterfront or Pike Place spots, and 2120 has no water at all; for a beach in Seattle a local would point to Alki or Shilshole.

maine-lobster.reason: These are solid, well-known Portland lobster spots (Luke's, Portland Lobster Co, DiMillo's, Bite Into Maine), a fair stand-in for a statewide ask, though Eventide and the coastal shacks are absent.

missing: Binondo / Ongpin Street food crawl stalls

tijuana-tacos.reason: Only #1 (Tacos el Nuevo Poblano) is a taco specialist; the rest are torta shops, a bar, a tlayuda place and a burrito stand with 15 reviews.

tokyo-vegan-no-in.reason: Nearly all are dedicated vegan restaurants a vegan traveler would recognize, such as Jangara Harajuku, Veggie Sushi and Vegan Eat Tokyo; only the marshmallow counter is marginal.

ba-vegan-capital.reason: These are mostly dedicated vegan spots in central Buenos Aires, including Mudrá, La Reverde and Konu, with Green Eat as the only non-vegan health chain.

arcadia-shaved-ice.reason: No shaved-ice or Taiwanese dessert shop appears; the list is ice cream, a burger stand, a Burmese restaurant, a bakery and frozen yogurt, in the San Gabriel Valley where shaved-ice shops are plentiful.

positano-pasta.reason: Too many results are outside Positano (a Sant'Agnello place 4.8 mi away across the peninsula, an Agerola pizzeria, a Praiano bar), and #1 is a 66-review snack shop, while Positano's known pasta tables are missing.

barcelona-couples.reason: The list is niche workshops and spas (ceramics, color analysis, massage) and a minor garden, and it misses the iconic romantic spots couples actually go to.

nyc-statue-view.reason: The search centered on Midtown, where no place can see the Statue of Liberty; only ONE Dine (#8) has that view.

nyc-propose.reason: The Boathouse, ROBERT and Electric Lemon fit, but Avra, Soothr and Bar 54 have no romantic view, and the classic view-proposal restaurants are missing.

vegas-burgers.reason: These are all burger specialists, led by Gordon Ramsay Burger, Black Tap and well-rated local spots such as Stay Tuned and Sickies, which is a fair Vegas burger list.

la-kbbq.reason: Most are real Koreatown grill-at-table spots, including Park's BBQ, Quarters and Road to Seoul; only #1 (a rice-bowl counter) is off.

nyc-empire-bridge.reason: Nubeluz and Magic Hour do overlook the Empire State Building, but ROBERT faces Central Park, Aurora and Aska in Williamsburg have no such view, and the Brooklyn Bridge view restaurants are absent.

london-farmers.reason: These are real London farmers' markets (Marylebone, Pimlico Road, Islington, South Kensington) plus Borough Market, though most are closed today since they run on weekends.

pasadena-late.reason: The first three satisfy the late-night filter, but only three Pasadena places came back, and the fourth is 18.8 mi away near LAX with a 2.5 rating.

near-from-here.reason: These are genuinely the restaurants within 0.2 mi of the traveler, which answers the ask, although no ratings or hours are shown to help choose.

hilton-manhattan.reason: It ignored which Hilton and centered on Columbus Circle, which no Hilton is near, and the unrated list looks stale: Asiate and Landmarc there have closed, and Ichimura at Brushstroke is a downtown venue.

g-locals-shibuya.reason: The top two are a board game café and the Shibuya Crossing viewing deck; the remainder are plausible casual spots (Keika ramen, oden) but nothing a local would single out.

g-authentic-pho.reason: These are all genuine pho shops across the San Gabriel Valley at reasonable distances, though the best-known local Vietnamese spot is absent.

g-sf-moscone-late.reason: All five really are open until 11 PM or later today and sit within about a mile of Moscone; it is a short but fair late-night list.

g-hk-quick-lunch.reason: Yat Lok and TamJai fit, but Arbor (three-Michelin-star) and Bo Innovation are tasting-menu fine dining, the opposite of a quick lunch.

g-rome-gf.reason: Every result is a dedicated gluten-free restaurant, pizzeria or bakery in central Rome.

g-seoul-halal.reason: Every result is halal, both around Myeongdong and City Hall and in the Itaewon halal hub (EID, Kervan), which is exactly the ask.

g-singapore-business.reason: Most are credible business-dinner venues (Peach Garden at OCBC, Artemis, Lerouy, 15 Stamford, private dining), though #1 is a catering and wedding listing and the hotel Cantonese standards are absent.

g-sf-third-wave.reason: These are mostly real specialty coffee shops near Union Square (The Coffee Movement, Home Coffee Roasters, Scullery), although the original third-wave landmark nearby is missing.

g-seoul-aesthetic.reason: The outdoor-patio requirement was ignored (#1 is a basement café) and the list is generic central cafés, missing the famous photogenic hanok and courtyard cafés nearby.

g-marais-bakery.reason: There are solid Marais bakery and coffee picks (The French Bastards, Bo&Mie, Rose Bakery, GRAVE, Kozy), with only the Le Pain Quotidien chain being filler.

g-austin-cold-brew.reason: These are just the nearest downtown cafés, several with few reviews, and the word 'brew' pulled in a brewery (Central District Brewing); nothing shows any cold-brew reputation.

missing: The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens

g-mbs-hidden.reason: Matches the words literally: a crystal shop called 'Secret', a gem museum and a business called 'HIDDEN'. None is an actual lesser-known sight near Marina Bay Sands.

g-dallas-after-5.reason: 'After 5 pm' isn't acted on. Six of eight close at or before 5 PM, and three are the same 411 Elm St site, so only Museum of Illusions and Reunion Tower work in the evening.

g-tokyo-speakeasy.reason: Almost none are speakeasies: #1 is a café terrace that closes at 8 PM, followed by craft-beer bars, a Belgian beer bar and a burger joint around Kanda. Only Bar Akamon and JANAI COFFEE come close.

g-bellagio-running.reason: There are no real paths at the Strip, so parks 2-6 miles away with trails (Sunset Park is the usual local answer) are a fair response, though the 3.3-rated Pecos-McLeod trailhead is a weak #2.

g-vancouver-hikes.reason: All are genuine North Shore and Pacific Spirit trails, including the Grouse Grind and Baden Powell, though low-review trailheads lead and several signature hikes are absent.

g-orlando-kids.reason: Half the list is escape rooms and game-show rooms aimed at adults, plus a 3.8-rated mirror maze. Orlando's classic family attractions outside the theme parks are missing.

g-restroom-near.reason: After Newcastle Park, the list is six duplicate, unnamed 'Bathroom' / 'Male Bathroom' / 'Female Bathroom' pins about 1 mi away at the mall. Arcadia County Park, 0.2 mi away with public restrooms, is missed.

g-station-restroom.reason: Returns Shinjuku Station itself, its exits and nearby stations, not where the restrooms inside the station are, so the traveler learns nothing new.

g-atm-fees.reason: The fee requirement is ignored: #1 is a merchant-services company rather than an ATM, and the list includes a Bitcoin ATM and a gas-station ATM, which carry the highest fees. Only the Chase and Citibank ATMs fit.

g-exchange-weekend.reason: Myeongdong and Insadong private money changers (MoneyBox and others) are exactly where locals send travelers. Only weekday hours are shown and there are no distances, so weekend opening isn't confirmed.

g-best-rates.reason: Only two results: a crypto ATM and a check-cashing/remittance shop. Neither is a place to get good currency-exchange rates.
missing: Chase, Bank of America or Wells Fargo branches (foreign currency orders)

g-supermarket.reason: Trader Joe's, ALDI, Ralphs, Vons and Grocery Outlet within about 2 mi are a fine answer. The odd #1 is a 1-review 'Whole Foods Bakery' sub-listing 2.2 mi away.

g-adapter.reason: It returns generic malls, many 7-13 miles away, plus night markets (one closed today) instead of stores that actually stock travel adapters; only the nearby Santa Anita mall is somewhat useful.

g-organic-grocery.reason: Only La Vie Claire is an organic store. The rest are generic minimarkets and late-night shops, and the 'nearest first' order is broken (a 3-review shop 1.4 mi away is #1).

g-milan-shopping-street.reason: The Galleria and Porta Nuova fit, but the rest are souvenir kiosks and a minimarket, and Milan's actual famous shopping streets are absent.

g-happy-hour.reason: The bars-only filter leaks: #1 is a coffee shop that closes at 6 PM, and a steakhouse, a burger-and-lobster restaurant and a diner sit among the few real bars (BXL, The Long Room, AperiBar).

g-vegan-dessert.reason: Only Chaumont Vegan and Val's Vegan Bake Shop are dessert-focused. Two Indian restaurants (#6, #7) and general vegan restaurants and cafés fill the rest.

g-library.reason: Arcadia, Monrovia, Temple City and nearby public libraries, nearest first, open this evening: exactly the answer.

g-first-date.reason: The traveler said 'not loud bars', yet the app applied a bars-only filter and returned Irish pubs, brewery taprooms and dive-style bars. That is the opposite of the ask, with only Zig Zag Café and Deep Dive plausible.

g-boba-date.reason: The real Diamond Jamboree and Irvine boba shops (Sunright, 7 Leaves, Jam Jam, TP Tea, Tastea). Seating isn't verified, and Sul & Beans is more of a bingsu café.

g-interactive-date.reason: Exactly what was asked: Lucky Strike bowling, Holey Moley, Puttshack and several mini-golf courses in and around Denver.

g-pottery.reason: All are Brooklyn ceramics studios that run wheel classes, nearest first, which is a fair answer for a couples class.

g-board-game-cafe.reason: Snakes & Lattes, The Guild House and Juju are real Toronto board-game cafés. A couple of entries (Pinochio dessert café, Understory) are uncertain fits.

g-anniversary.reason: Upscale, reservation-taking romantic picks (Arpège, Boutary, La Calèche, Le Sergent Recruteur on Île Saint-Louis), fitting for an anniversary. Le P'tit Piano and the hotel tea room are lighter.

g-budget-date.reason: Well-loved, affordable-but-special Covent Garden and Soho spots (Dishoom, Kricket, Speedboat Bar, Le Garrick, Mildreds), all priced $$ as filtered.
